answer: At most 2 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a opal tag. The vertex cap is checked at intake and crystal shows the per-origin counts. A datacenter or proxy pool as a result cannot mint a army of identities in one epoch regardless of capital it holds, because each identity consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. That is 15 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
